reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm each batch refund exists in the refunds table with the same amount. I'll start by listing the refunds.
All three batch refunds appear in the refunds table with matching amounts, so I can proceed. I need the customer list from the orders before I can get net balances.
All three batch refunds match the refunds table, so I can proceed. The orders list shows three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get acme's net balance first.
Acme's net of 21583 matches orders 280 and 283 (37804) minus refund 283 (16221), so the figure checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 19734 matches orders 281 and 284 (27743) minus refund 281 (8009). Acme also checked out. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 41045 matches orders 282 and 285 (46386) minus refund 285 (5341). All three customers reconcile and every batch refund is in the refunds table, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 21583 is recorded. Next is birch, whose net balance I already confirmed as 19734 against its orders and batch refund 281.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt is the last customer, with net 41045 that matches orders 282 and 285 minus refund 285, so I'll record its payout now.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each net balance matched the orders minus the batch refund, and every batch refund was in the refunds table with the same amount.
